assessments.reason: Re-reviewed official RustSec RUSTSEC-2026-0370 against database 3279c99911354c400e1d41e47c7d60e39258b147 on 2026-10-27: this is an informational/unmaintained standalone-crate notice, not a vulnerability or patched standalone release. The exact SHA-256-bound application lock uses zvariant 5.15.1 through the updated zbus/zbus_macros 5.19.0 stack. Notification (notify-rust 4.18.2), portal (ashpd 0.11.1/rfd 0.16.1) and OS-vault (secret-service 5.2.0/zbus-secret-service-keyring-store 1.0.1) consumers still independently constrain zbus 5; forcing only a direct zbus 6 update does not remove them. See docs/ZBUS-MAINTENANCE-REVIEW.md. Whole-lock scanning keeps this warning visible; changed lock bytes, versions, vulnerability/unsound findings or expiry fail closed. Reassessment remains due 2026-11-15, without extension. Source: https://github.com/RustSec/advisory-db/blob/3279c99911354c400e1d41e47c7d60e39258b147/crates/zvariant/RUSTSEC-2026-0370.md

The patched builder removes RPM OpenPGP entirely. Remaining RSA 0.9.10 has exactly one parent, tauri-macos-sign 2.4.3 (crate SHA256 4478507a7aeee53b73ac780f4f645a584ae07eab599a3d171f8afb258fb02026), gated to macOS in both CLI and bundler manifests. Re-reviewed official source revision 993038c49185307dfc895ab7657d77ca0d5ed7c7 on 2026-10-27: certificate.rs:835-868 only generates a fresh RSA key and serializes it for a local self-signed test certificate; it does not call RSA decryption affected by the Marvin advisory. Linux/Windows builders do not compile that dependency. Canonical builds reject signing credentials and isolated updater signing uses Minisign Ed25519. Whole-lock scanning still reports this exact expiring advisory; no upstream RSA patch or advisory exclusion is claimed. Reassessment remains due 2026-11-15 without extension. Source: https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/993038c49185307dfc895ab7657d77ca0d5ed7c7/crates/tauri-macos-sign/src/apple_codesign/certificate.rs
